newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate panel clears D.C. homebuyer tax credit.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate panel clears D.C. homebuyer tax credit.

text.p: The Senate Finance Committee late Thursday approved an amendment to tax-cut legislation that would allow District of Columbia residents to take a $5,000 tax credit on the purchase of their first homes.
Aides to Sen. Connie Mack, R-Fla., sponsor of the amendment, were unavailable for comment. The overall tax cut bill won committee approval near midnight by an 18-2 vote.
The panel rejected 11-9 a proposal by Vermont Republican Jim Jeffords to strike from the bill a series of tax incentives for D.C. businesses.
Jeffords proposed replacing them with a trust fund for school renovations in the financially strapped city.
Under the remaining tax incentives, certain D.C. communities with a poverty level greater than 35 percent would be desigated as a new D.C. Enterprise Zone.
Businesses in the zone would be eligible for expanded tax-exempt bond financing and a 20 percent tax credit on wages paid to poor workers.
The committee-passed bill also would exclude capital gains requiremenets for new investment in D.C. businesses that are held for at least five years and meet certain standards.
It also would provide $75 million in tax credits to banks and other lenders that provide equity and loans to D.C. businesses in poor areas.
